2rc2dk:182: . The core insight of this article lies in revealing the multi-agent architecture philosophy that "specialization beats generalization." When a single Agent tries to take on all functions, it simultaneously suffers from context pollution (attention scattered across heterogeneous tasks), skill conflicts (the principle of least privilege is violated), and persona conflicts (drastically different behavioral patterns struggle to coexist). npjlve:210: . The author divides OpenClaw's memory into three levels: short-term (session context), medium-term (work logs from recent days), and long-term (cross-session knowledge accumulation). This design directly corresponds to the trichotomy of working memory, episodic memory, and semantic memory in human cognition. Traditional monolithic Agents lack a stable memory persistence mechanism, causing every session to start from scratch; the three-tier memory architecture enables Agents to accumulate experience and achieve truly continuous work. This point is repeatedly emphasized in both the investment assistant and development assistant configurations—both treat "remembering work patterns" as a core configuration goal.
